archived_trends.name: Dubai as a Competitive Tax Jurisdiction
archived_trends.summary: Dubai offers a 9% corporate tax rate, with 0% rates in Free Zones, and allows for 100% foreign ownership, positioning itself as a business-friendly hub.
archived_trends.evidence: Dubai has a 9% corporate tax, with 0% rate in Free Zones.

archived_trends.name: Austria's Income Tax Reduction
archived_trends.summary: Austria is planning to reduce its top income tax rate from 55% to 50% in 2026, potentially impacting labor markets and investment.
archived_trends.evidence: Austria is planning to eliminate its highest tax bracket in 2026.

archived_trends.name: US Corporate Tax Implications of Global Minimum Tax
archived_trends.summary: The US is positioned to collect additional tax revenue from its companies if they pay less than 15% in other jurisdictions, potentially impacting the competitiveness of US-based MNEs. The side-by-side arrangement exempts US companies from full Pillar Two compliance.
archived_trends.evidence: The plan would effectively allow the US to tax the difference between the 15% minimum rate and lower rates paid in countries like Ireland. US side-by-side arrangement exempts US companies from full Pillar Two compliance.

archived_trends.name: Legal Challenges to US Tariffs
archived_trends.summary: The legality of tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) is being challenged in court, creating uncertainty for businesses and trade policy. The Supreme Court is expected to rule in the coming months.
archived_trends.evidence: Court for International Trade (CIT) ruled IEEPA tariffs unlawful. Supreme Court expected to rule in coming months.

archived_trends.name: Corporate Tax Rate Adjustments - Portugal
archived_trends.summary: Portugal is planning to decrease its corporate income tax rate by one percentage point per year from 2026 to 2028.
archived_trends.evidence: Corporate income tax will decrease by one percentage point per year, starting from January 2026 and ending in 2028.

archived_trends.name: ASEAN Corporate Tax Rates
archived_trends.summary: Corporate tax rates vary across ASEAN countries, with Singapore maintaining one of the lowest rates in the region.
archived_trends.evidence: ASEAN countries have differing corporate tax rates, ranging from 17% in Singapore to 20% or higher in other member states.

archived_trends.name: Singapore E-invoicing Mandate (InvoiceNow)
archived_trends.summary: Singapore's nationwide e-invoicing initiative, InvoiceNow, is expanding to include GST-registered businesses, becoming a core component of its digital tax transformation. Compliance deadlines are being phased in.
archived_trends.evidence: InvoiceNow is based on the Peppol framework and requires structured invoice data submission to IRAS. Phased compliance deadlines are expanding mandatory participation.

archived_trends.name: ASEAN Corporate Tax Rate Variation
archived_trends.summary: Corporate tax rates vary across ASEAN countries, with Singapore maintaining one of the lowest rates in the region.
archived_trends.evidence: ASEAN countries have differing corporate tax rates, ranging from 17% in Singapore to 20% or higher in other member states.

archived_trends.name: Singapore as a Competitive Tax Jurisdiction
archived_trends.summary: Singapore maintains a competitive corporate tax environment with a 17% rate, attractive exemptions, and rebates, enhancing its appeal for foreign investment.
archived_trends.evidence: Singapore's corporate income tax rate is 17%, with various rebates and exemptions available. It employs a one-tier taxation system.

archived_trends.name: Corporate GST/HST Updates
archived_trends.summary: Updates to Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) regulations are impacting businesses, requiring attention to collection, remittance, and reporting procedures.
archived_trends.evidence: Businesses are responsible for collecting and remitting GST/HST, and claiming input tax credits. Updates to rates and regulations are ongoing.

archived_trends.name: GST Implications on Corporate Guarantees
archived_trends.summary: The application of GST to corporate guarantees is gaining attention, requiring businesses to understand the implications of these transactions.
archived_trends.evidence: Corporate guarantees provided without a specific fee attract GST, calculated as 1% of the guarantee amount. If a fee is charged, GST is applied to the actual fee amount.
